entries.name: Author-recipient-topic model
entries.definition: A generative message model with a topic distribution for each ordered sender-recipient pair, in which each word selects a recipient uniformly from the message's observed recipient set, a topic from that pair, and a word from the selected topic.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to McCallum, Corrada-Emmanuel and Wang's ART model in the December 2004 technical report and IJCAI 2005 paper. Sender and recipient have distinct roles in selecting a pair-specific topic vector. The model differs from author-topic modeling over undifferentiated participants, document-specific LDA, network-edge generation and the later latent-role RART variants. ART is a source acronym within this scope, not a universal expansion of that acronym. limitations: The corpus-probability display on report p.4 factors separately integrated document marginals despite shared random parameters. The subsequent corpus-count derivation on p.5 preserves sharing. The record uses the shared model and qualifies that display; no failure of unseen implementation is inferred.

Pair-specific parameters can be weakly informed for sparse or unobserved pairs. Fixed topic count, uniform recipient selection, stationary pair preferences, finite vocabulary and bag-of-words emissions constrain the model. Suggestions to smooth toward sender-only vectors are not part of the basic specification.

Reported role similarities use descriptive topic distributions, divergence matrices and selected email examples with manual entity resolution and heuristic text cleaning. They do not establish universal predictive superiority, actual job roles, expertise or causal social relationships. Topic and role labels remain interpretations.

RART introduces additional latent sender/recipient roles and has token-level and message-level variants. It is a distinct extension; preliminary staged fitting after fixing an ART sample is not full joint posterior inference. No author code, email corpus or benchmark was executed.

claims.statement: For a fixed topic count and vocabulary, each topic has a categorical word distribution phi_z with a Dirichlet prior, and each ordered sender-recipient pair (a,r) has a topic vector theta_ar with a Dirichlet prior. Given sender a_d and nonempty observed recipient set R_d, each token selects x uniformly from R_d, z from theta_(a_d,x), and w from phi_z. Conditional on these parameters, the message topic mixture averages the eligible pair vectors. The reversed pair can have a different vector. Sender identity, recipient sets and message lengths are conditioned on; this direction-sensitive content model does not itself generate network edges or establish causal influence.

claims.statement: Integrating the shared pair-topic and topic-word vectors gives a collapsed token update. For eligible recipient r, topic z and observed word v, its weight is proportional to (n_(a_d,r),z^(-i)+alpha_z)/(n_(a_d,r),.^(-i)+sum(alpha)) times (n_zv^(-i)+beta_v)/(n_z.^(-i)+sum(beta)). Counts exclude the token and pool the corpus; the uniform recipient factor cancels among eligible choices. Joint recipient/topic sampling or compatible separate conditional updates target the collapsed assignment posterior. Finite samples approximate posterior summaries and do not certify convergence. Sharing random parameters across messages requires joint corpus integration; a product of separately integrated message marginals is generally different.

entries.definition: A generative sequence model combining an HMM class sequence with a document topic mixture, where one designated class emits words through latent topics and each other class emits words from its own categorical distribution.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to the composite model of Griffiths, Steyvers, Blei and Tenenbaum's Integrating Topics and Syntax. limitations: The distinction between syntactic classes and semantic topics is induced by this model and corpus. It need not coincide with linguistic ground truth, supervised part-of-speech tags or full grammar. Fixed class/topic counts and finite-state local transitions restrict its scope.

The source LDA comparison uses a semantic class plus a dedicated sentence-marker class with the stated boundary handling; arbitrary two-state HMMs are not equivalent to LDA. With one topic, the semantic emission has its own prior, so the resulting HMM comparison must preserve those hyperparameters.

A finite auxiliary-update invariance calculation supports a compatible semantic-only interpretation; it is not a proof that historical software followed that convention or that finite chains mixed. The displayed first-order transition formula requires additional factors for higher-order contexts.

Historical results use particular Brown, TASA and NIPS preparations. Adjusted Rand agreement is not supervised tag accuracy, and the reported harmonic-mean evidence estimate is not exact marginal likelihood or guaranteed stable. The document-classification experiment reports LDA somewhat better. No universal advantage or empirical reproduction is asserted.

claims.statement: A document draws a Dirichlet topic vector. An HMM generates the token-class sequence. If a token occupies the designated semantic class, a topic selected from the document vector determines its word distribution; otherwise its class-specific word distribution generates the token. The Bayesian formulation puts symmetric Dirichlet priors on topic emissions, nonsemantic class emissions and transition rows. The source draws a topic at every position, but topics unused by nonsemantic emissions can be marginalized. The displayed model is first order; experiments also use higher-order transitions and a dedicated sentence-marker state. Initial and boundary conventions, class count, topic count and vocabulary are part of a complete specification.

evidence.locator: Sections 2.1-2.2, PDF pp.3-4, Figure 1, generative steps and prior definitions

claims.statement: The source alternates topic and class updates with parameters integrated out. Its document-topic counts include semantic tokens only, and the first-order class update accounts for both neighboring transitions, including corrections when they share a transition row or cell. A coherent interpretation first marginalizes unused topics, then introduces a temporary topic for the currently updated nonsemantic token from the leave-one-out document predictive law. Updating that topic and then the class allows the common document-topic factor to cancel in the class conditional; discard the temporary topic if the resulting class is nonsemantic. This is an explicit curator interpretation of the printed count convention, checked in a small enumerated model, not a claim about unseen author code. Retaining all inactive topic draws in a fully augmented sampler would instead require document counts over all those draws.

entries.definition: A generative document model in which one Dirichlet-distributed membership vector mixes aspect-specific word distributions for an abstract and aspect-specific reference distributions for its bibliography.

limitations: The main model treats references as multinomial draws with replacement although observed bibliographies are represented by presence indicators. Bernoulli inclusion models that use absent references and publication-time restrictions are discussed on pp.4-5 as alternatives; they are not the fitted multinomial model.

The p.4 display labels its integrated document likelihood p(theta|d), but it is not a posterior over parameters. Conditional independence given memberships is stronger than exchangeability alone. Shared latent proportions explain modeled dependence, not causal citation relationships or objectively true scientific disciplines.

Reported results concern a selected PNAS Biological Sciences 1997-2001 corpus and a chosen eight-aspect fit. Topic counts were compared informally, and aspect interpretations used high-probability words/references. Neither universal model-selection optimality nor recovery of a unique semantic partition follows.

An unweighted average of document loadings does not generally equal a pooled token-level percentage when document lengths differ. Source figure cross-references are inconsistent: use the actual Figure 1 on preprint p.9 and Table 4 on p.13. No source implementation or benchmark was executed.

claims.statement: For fixed K aspects, each aspect has a categorical word distribution and a separate categorical reference-ID distribution. Each document draws lambda from Dirichlet(alpha). Conditional on lambda, its word tokens are sampled from the lambda-weighted word mixture and its reference entries from the lambda-weighted reference mixture, with channel lengths conditioned on. Equivalently, each word or reference draws its own aspect label from the same lambda. The document likelihood integrates the product of both channel likelihoods over lambda; their conditional independence does not imply marginal independence. Removing the reference observations yields a word-only LDA-type model, whereas fixed rather than random membership vectors give a PLSA-style alternative.

notes: All six pages of author-hosted IJCAI 2005 paper visually read, including all tables, figures and bibliography. No numeric printed page labels visible; use PDF locators.

ART conditions on an observed sender and a nonempty recipient set. Each ordered sender-recipient pair has a topic vector with Dirichlet prior; each topic has a categorical word law with Dirichlet prior. For each token, select a recipient uniformly from the observed set, then topic from the ordered pair, then word. The model is direction-sensitive because theta_ar and theta_ra are distinct, not because it models causal influence.

Despite prose about modeling the social network, the displayed joint conditions on sender/recipient metadata and does not generate edges, recipient sets or message counts. Conditional word law averages pair-topic distributions over recipients. It is not ordinary AT applied to an undifferentiated participant set, nor graph-based role clustering itself.

Paper states Gibbs sampling was used, referring to the 2004 technical report for details; no unseen collapsed update is asserted yet. Author index leads to a 16-page December 11 2004 report and 24-page 2007 journal version, neither fully read at this checkpoint.

Pages 3-5 compare descriptive topic distributions and selected role-similarity examples using inverse Jensen-Shannon matrices and graph clustering. Topic names are author interpretations. The paper does not report a generally validated causal-role or universal predictive-superiority theorem; example pairs and manual email coreference affect conclusions.

Pages 5-6 separately introduce RART variants: token-level sender and recipient roles in RART1, message-level roles in RART2, and a possible shared recipient role. These are distinct latent-role extensions, not aliases for ART. The preliminary RART1 experiment freezes a single ART sample of topics and recipients before fitting roles, so it is not full joint posterior sampling. A separate provisional cohort should retain those variants.

Author-index metadata distinguishes IJCAI 2005 from 2004 technical report and 2007 journal paper; date claims about the actual inspected bytes must follow the title pages. No author code or corpus inspected/executed.

All eight official NIPS 2004 pages visually read, figures and bibliography included. Often cited as 2005 proceedings publication; use official conference year and exact inspected version. No visible numeric page labels; use PDF locators.

Sections 2-2.1 define a composite model: an HMM class sequence selects whether each emission uses a class-specific word law or a semantic topic mixture. One class (c=1) is semantic; each document has a Dirichlet topic vector, topic/class emissions and transition rows have symmetric Dirichlet priors in the Bayesian version. Unlike independent mixture gating, all tokens follow HMM class transitions; unlike a product of experts, nonsemantic tokens use only their class emission.

Generative process draws a topic for every token but uses it only for semantic-class emissions. Marginalizing unused topics yields the equivalent semantic-only latent representation. HMM start/boundary conventions must be specified; the experiment dedicates a state to sentence markers and explores first through third orders. Fixed topic/class counts and finite vocabulary remain.

The printed topic update uses semantic-token-only document counts despite the fully augmented generative story drawing unused topics at other positions. A coherent interpretation marginalizes all unused topics, introduces a fresh auxiliary topic for the currently updated nonsemantic token using the leave-one-out document predictive law, samples topic then class, and discards the topic if the class remains nonsemantic. The document-topic factor then cancels in the class conditional because the auxiliary law is shared between class alternatives. A 27-state, three-token finite calculation confirms posterior invariance to floating-point precision for each local update, and confirms the two-edge transition correction. This is a curator interpretation and finite validation, not inspection of author implementation or a global mixing guarantee. Literal retention of every inactive topic would instead require all-topic document counts.

The first-order class-transition factor includes indicator corrections when outgoing/incoming transitions share a row or cell; a simple product of two independently smoothed transitions is not generally the collapsed conditional. The source says higher-order models add corresponding terms, not that this displayed formula covers arbitrary order.

The LDA endpoint uses a semantic state plus a sentence-marker state and fixed boundary handling, not every arbitrary two-state HMM. The T=1 endpoint gives an HMM with a distinct prior for its semantic emission. Model composition differs from the model labels claimed by fitting outcomes.

Results depend on Brown/TASA/NIPS corpora, unknown-word replacement, fixed counts, finite chains and sampled hyperparameters. Syntactic versus semantic allocation changes by corpus, e.g. model/algorithm can be assigned to syntax in NIPS. This is not universal linguistic truth or full grammar induction.

Section 3.3 estimates evidence with a harmonic mean of likelihoods from late MCMC samples; it is not exact marginal likelihood and can be unstable. POS evaluation uses adjusted Rand index, not direct supervised tagging accuracy. Section 3.5 classifies with naive Bayes on topic features and reports LDA somewhat better, not universal composite superiority. No corpus, implementation or benchmark was executed.

Provisional references include distributional syntactic clustering (Redington/Chater/Finch), syntactic/semantic predictor combinations (Coccaro/Jurafsky), harmonic-mean evidence estimation and adjusted Rand index; assess identities and prior frontier before adding leads.

All 13 author-hosted preprint pages visually read, including bibliography and late tables. Printed page labels equal PDF pages 1-13, not final PNAS 5220-5227. Paper has some cross-reference typos: the histogram is Figure 1 p.9 and the mean-loadings display is Table 4 p.13, despite prose saying Figure 4.

The broad mixed-membership framework pp.2-3 includes fixed or random membership vectors and multiple response distributions. The selected document model pp.3-4 is narrower: a shared document Dirichlet vector mixes two sets of multinomial aspect distributions, one for abstract words and one for bibliography reference IDs. Each token/reference may use a different aspect; it is not one document-level latent class.

Equations 7-11 p.4 integrate the shared Dirichlet mixture over products of word/reference probabilities raised to observed counts. The displayed p(theta|d) is used as a likelihood in theta; the expression is a document likelihood conditional on parameters, not a parameter posterior. Document lengths and vocabularies are conditioned, and no token-to-reference alignment or citation causation is modeled.

Conditional independence given membership does not imply marginal independence; both channels share the latent vector. Exchangeability alone is weaker than conditional independence, despite loose wording in the source. Marginalizing the references recovers a word-only LDA-type model, while fixed document memberships give a PLSA-style counterpart; shared random membership differentiates this from fitting two independent topic models.

The main model samples references multinomially with replacement although observed bibliography indicators are 0/1. Pages 4-5 propose Bernoulli reference alternatives that incorporate absence and discuss publication-time restrictions; these are not the model fitted in the reported study. Broad model class and proposed alternatives should not be silently substituted for the demonstrated two-channel model.

Estimating the Model p.5 uses a variational approximation for the displayed results and discusses expectation propagation as an alternative. Exact finite integrals can be expanded but cost grows rapidly; the prose cannot-compute-explicitly is a practical tractability claim, not mathematical nonexistence. No global optimum or universal EP superiority follows. Full implementation equations/code are not supplied here.

Results pp.5-10,12-13 concern a selected Biological Sciences PNAS 1997-2001 corpus. Authors compare eight versus ten aspects informally and report eight for interpretability; no general criterion proves eight optimal. Learned aspect labels are post hoc interpretations of words/references, with interpretation help from a biologist. Official categories are comparison metadata rather than supervised targets.

Posterior document loadings use approximate Dirichlet means. Averaging loadings across papers weights documents equally and does not automatically equal the fraction of all pooled word tokens from an aspect; the wording around 29 percent on pp.9-10 needs qualification. Sparse estimated priors, vocabulary selection, bibliography simplifications and topic label nonidentifiability limit interpretation. No claim that recovered aspects are objectively true disciplines or evidence of causal interdisciplinary influence.

References pp.10-11 lead to Grade of Membership, Dirichlet latent-class generalizations, admixture/population structure, Cohn-Hofmann joint text/hypertext and Barnard et al matching words/pictures. Deduplicate these against maintained records/frontier before creating cohorts. No author code or corpus executed.

All 16 pages of author-hosted Technical Report UM-CS-2004-096 visually read, including equations, tables, graphs and references. Title page says December 11, 2004; printed and PDF pages agree. Do not assign a January 2005 revision date from a different copy.

Section 2 pp.2-4 and Figure 1 p.3 specify ordered-pair topic mixtures and observed sender/recipient metadata. Pair distributions may be smoothed toward author-only mixtures as a suggestion, not part of the demonstrated basic model. Treating one sender as AT author is not document-specific LDA unless each document has a unique sender.

Section 2.1 pp.4-6 derives corpus-level Dirichlet integrations and collapsed word-topic/ordered-pair-topic counts. The joint recipient/topic conditional is proportional to the leave-one-out pair-topic predictive factor times topic-word predictive factor; recipient choice is restricted to the observed set and its uniform factor cancels. Separate recipient and topic updates also require consistent leave-one-out counts; p.6 abbreviates the removal subscripts.

The final displayed corpus expression on p.4 multiplies single-document probabilities after separately integrating shared theta/phi. That is not the general corpus marginal when shared random parameters couple documents; integrate the corpus likelihood jointly. The subsequent corpus-count derivation p.5 uses global sharing. This is a printed-expression qualification, not evidence that unseen code used the wrong objective.

Sampling approximates posterior expectations; exact conditional algebra does not imply a finite chain has converged. No universal exact-inference impossibility claim: finite state enumeration exists in small cases. Author code was not inspected or run.

Section 4 pp.6-12 and Figure 3 p.13 show selected email corpora and illustrative comparisons with AT/network similarity. Entity aliases were manually merged and quoted text heuristically removed; one reported author-alias discovery reflects a preprocessing omission. Pair similarity and interpreted clusters are not a validated prediction of actual job roles, expertise or causality. No universal superiority follows from these examples.

Section 5 pp.12,14-15 and Figure 4 p.15 describe RART1 token roles, RART2 message-level sender/individual recipient roles, RART3 a common recipient role. Only RART1 generative details are developed, and Section 6 explicitly calls the experiments preliminary. Freezing topics from an ART sample gives a conditional staged procedure, not integrated joint RART posterior inference.

References p.16 include McCallum 1999 multi-label mixture model, stochastic blockmodels, structural equivalence and Wolfe-Jensen overlapping role factor models. Keep separate identities and check existing coverage before adding leads.

limitations: The number of topics is finite and fixed in this construction. Integrating a continuous Dirichlet mixture does not introduce infinitely many topic classes. Infinite exchangeability supports the representation discussed in Section 3.1; arbitrary finite exchangeability alone is not the asserted theorem.

Given observed topic assignments, Dirichlet conjugacy is exact. With topics unobserved, the marginal posterior over proportions is generally not a single Dirichlet; gamma=alpha+expected counts is a variational update, not exact marginal conjugacy. Exact inference is generally difficult, and bound optimization need not monotonically improve the true likelihood or attain its global maximum.

The basic model ignores word order and explicit within-topic dependencies, though integrating document proportions induces dependence between tokens. Zero word probabilities require smoothing or other support handling for novel documents. A prior over document mixtures does not guarantee freedom from overfitting, identifiable topics or meaningful semantic labels.

The Bayesian topic-prior extension requires expected log topic probabilities in its assignment update. The appendix’s printed alpha Hessian has a sign/factor mismatch with the preceding gradient; the consistent Hessian is M*(trigamma(sum alpha)-delta_ij*trigamma(alpha_i)). This record does not adopt that printed Hessian as verified code. Equation (13) correctly uses the normalized posterior.

The comparison’s empirical mixture over training-document indices must weight an entire document once; the printed p(d) inside its token product is not adopted. These mathematical qualifications do not establish an error in unseen author software or experiments.

The source’s document, classification and recommendation experiments have distinct protocols. No exact likelihood replication, generic performance advantage or biological-mechanism conclusion is claimed. All source material concerns the specified 2003 model, not every later topic-model extension.

Given a document length N_d, draw z_dn~Categorical(theta_d) and w_dn~Categorical(B_zdn) for each token. Conditional on theta_d and B, token probabilities are sum_i theta_di*B_iw and tokens are independent; integrating theta_d gives p(w_d|alpha,B)=integral Dir(theta_d;alpha)*product_n(sum_i theta_di*B_i,w_dn)dtheta_d. This is an exchangeable document distribution, generally with dependent tokens after integration. An unordered count vector additionally includes its multinomial multiplicity. The paper’s Poisson length law is optional to this conditional construction. For fixed B, its mean-field approximation is q(theta,z)=Dir(theta;gamma)*product_n Cat(z_n;phi_n), with phi_ni proportional B_i,w_n*exp[digamma(gamma_i)-digamma(sum_j gamma_j)] and gamma_i=alpha_i+sum_n phi_ni. Variational EM optimizes the evidence lower bound, updating B from expected topic-word counts and alpha numerically. Section 5.4 separately places Dirichlet priors on B; then the assignment update uses expected log topic probabilities, not fixed B values.

The alias PLSI identifies this underlying model, not every cosine, interpolation or model-averaging choice in a retrieval pipeline. Tempered EM is one fitting procedure rather than part of the model’s defining probability law. Compared all 442 pinned AIO labels and scoped synonyms and 418 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. limitations: The base construction is a normalized distribution of indexed co-occurrences. It has no LDA-style population prior on new document mixtures; fold-in estimation is possible, so this is not a claim that unseen documents cannot be represented at all.

Training-document mixture parameters grow with the corpus. Maximum-likelihood or tempered fitting can overfit; local EM optimization, initialization and rank selection do not guarantee global optimality or unique factors. Permuting topic labels preserves the law, and linearly dependent topic distributions can yield nonunique mixture weights.

The bag-of-words representation omits token order and explicit within-topic word interactions. It is not a raw-count Poisson MRF, a canonical-parameter admixture, or a neural density estimator. Topic labels and selected high-probability words are interpretations, not verified semantic or causal categories.

Positive-count cells require positive modeled mass. Responsibility updates need nonzero denominators; unused components require a specified handling convention. Zero-count terms use the standard zero-contribution convention.

Historical retrieval experiments use particular corpora, ranks, held-out tempering and cosine interpolation. No universal retrieval advantage, exact new-document marginal likelihood or author implementation is certified.

claims.statement: For finite document indices d, vocabulary items w and K latent classes z, choose normalized nonnegative distributions pi_z, a_z(d) and b_z(w), and define p(d,w)=sum_z pi_z*a_z(d)*b_z(w). Given z, d and w are independent. Equivalently, for p(d)>0, p(w|d)=sum_z theta_dz*b_z(w), where theta_dz=pi_z*a_z(d)/p(d). Fit observed counts n(d,w) with sum_dw n(d,w)*log p(d,w). An exact EM E-step computes r_dwz=pi_z*a_z(d)*b_z(w)/p(d,w); M-steps normalize the corresponding count-weighted responsibilities over words, documents and classes. Each conditional document word distribution is an arithmetic convex combination of topic probabilities. In the original fold-in procedure, keep b_z(w) fixed and fit a new query or document’s mixture weights. This introduces new fitted weights rather than integrating over a population prior as in LDA.

Equation(26) uses the contemporaneous observation in a combined unary expression. In a general sequence, a delayed-state contribution must instead use the corresponding earlier observation; this cannot be repaired only by ignoring endpoints.

The prior remains first-order, but the conditioned hidden distribution generally has long-range interactions. A standard HMM forward–backward pass over the original single state is not automatically exact; exact inference can require an expanded state with cost growing with context width.

The Gaussian additive-mean, identity-covariance form is the inspected example, not a claim that every contextual emission distribution must have that form. The synthetic Figure1 uses five states and two-sided context rather than only the displayed binary one-sided specialization.

At hidden index j, the contribution through the delayed v term uses observation x_(j-Delta), when that observation lies within the valid window. Summing the normalized joint density over paths gives the observed likelihood. native_neighbors.identity_notes: PoHMM is Brown and Hinton’s undirected product construction with one hidden chain per expert. It is not a mixture that selects one HMM, an ordinary single-chain HMM, or a directed factorial HMM whose multiple latent chains jointly generate locally normalized emissions. Taylor and Hinton’s later AIS study retains this model identity and supplies an evaluation procedure, not a new synonymous architecture. The model is not restricted to linguistic sequences. limitations: The partition function depends on model parameters and sequence length. Separate forward–backward computations evaluate the unnormalized product and complete-data hidden posteriors; they do not by themselves give the product’s global normalizer or exact likelihood. Small finite models can be enumerated, but this does not establish scalable tractability.

When observations are missing or future observations are integrated out, the experts can become dependent. Exact separate posterior inference given a complete sequence is not a claim of equally simple causal prediction from a prefix.

CD learning is approximate, and the customary short-chain update is not generally an exact likelihood or contrastive-objective gradient. The Brown paper’s initial pseudocode writes probability derivatives where its final update uses log derivatives; this record follows the log-score update supported by the later explicit formulation.

Brown Equation (3) places a derivative outside a posterior expectation. The score identity used here means the expectation of the log-joint derivative at the current posterior, without differentiating through that posterior. The shared deterministic emission-feature extension is optional, not an extra required stochastic latent layer.

Taylor Section 3.3 estimates normalization with an AIS path that tempers emission potentials inside hidden-path sums. This is generally different from simply raising whole HMM marginal likelihoods to fractional powers. Approximate normalizer estimates, and their logarithms, are not exact log likelihoods or a universal reliability guarantee.

native_neighbors.name: Gibbs sampling
native_neighbors.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that repeatedly draws a coordinate or block from its full conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining coordinates.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes exact conditional resampling, including fixed coordinate cycles and fixed random-scan mixtures. It is a sampling procedure, not a Gibbs distribution, Markov random field, annealing schedule or conditional maximization method. Metropolis-within-Gibbs replaces some exact conditional draws by invariant transitions and is represented separately. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 159 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive full-checkout searches found prior discovery leads for Gibbs and slice sampling plus unrelated environment substring hits, not existing concept records. Existing HMM/MRF models and general Metropolis–Hastings were inspected to distinguish model, general transition and specialized algorithm scope.
limitations: The full conditional distributions must be compatible with a proper joint target and be sampled correctly. An approximate conditional draw is not automatically an exact Gibbs step.
Target invariance alone does not establish irreducibility, aperiodicity, convergence from every start or rapid mixing. Coordinate dependence and disconnected support can obstruct exploration.

The finite positive-state convergence theorem in Geman and Geman has explicit site-visit and positivity assumptions; it is not a theorem for every continuous, constrained or parallel Gibbs implementation.
Simultaneously updating dependent coordinates using stale neighbors is outside the stated sequential mechanism; valid parallel or adaptive scan schemes need separate arguments.
Fixed-temperature posterior sampling and a cooling schedule for optimization are different procedures. No universal convergence rate or image-restoration performance is asserted.

native_neighbors.name: Hierarchical mixture of experts
native_neighbors.definition: A conditional mixture-model family that organizes output experts as leaves of a tree and forms each leaf’s mixture weight by multiplying input-dependent probabilistic gates along its root-to-leaf path.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: The inspected Jordan–Jacobs construction uses generalized-linear experts and softmax gates with shared external input, with a finite tree defining nested soft partitions. It is static conditional modeling, distinct from temporal hidden Markov decision trees, hard classification trees, hierarchical clustering and language-specific sparse MoE routing. A mixture density network shares conditional-mixture semantics but need not impose this tree factorization or generalized-linear leaf structure. Flattening a fixed tree gives leaf weights without making every flat gating parameterization the same hierarchical model. EM, IRLS and the online surrogate are fitting procedures, not the model identity. limitations: The source uses soft gates that mix expert densities; it does not require hard routing, top-k sparse activation, a language model or a causal interpretation of the decision hierarchy.

Exact EM likelihood monotonicity requires a valid E-step and an M-step that increases the expected complete log likelihood under suitable regularity. It does not automatically apply to arbitrary gradient steps, the log-target least-squares surrogate or discounted online updates, and does not guarantee a global optimum.

claims.statement: For input x and leaf l, define w_l(x) as the product of normalized child-gate probabilities along the path to l. Then p(y|x)=sum_l w_l(x) p_l(y|x). In the two-level presentation, p(y|x)=sum_i g_i(x) sum_j g_(j|i)(x) p_ij(y|x), with softmax gates and generalized-linear conditional expert densities. The conditional output mean is the corresponding weighted sum of expert means. Given an observed y, leaf responsibilities are proportional to w_l(x) p_l(y|x); they condition on both x and y, unlike input-only gates. Conditional EM alternates these responsibilities with weighted expert fits and gate fits to soft multinomial targets; a lower gate’s objective is weighted by the posterior probability of reaching its parent. The paper uses IRLS inside those maximum-likelihood subproblems. Its separate Algorithm 2 instead regresses log responsibilities by least squares, and its online variant uses discounted recursive weighted least squares. Those surrogate procedures are approximations to the specified fitting approach.
